haiku-low.q1: Valid events are accepted and rejected ones are listed with reasons. 202 is returned only after the log acknowledges every accepted event in the batch.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes. Mobile keeps unacknowledged events up to 7 days.
haiku-low.q3: The winner is the copy with the lowest offset in its partition, the first durably accepted. Later copies are dropped and stay in the raw archive.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday's partition. Its day is the UTC day of received_at (00:10 Tuesday), and the client timestamp is never used for the day.
haiku-low.q5: A key-value store holds event_id mapped to partition:offset, set only if absent. Each key expires by per-key TTL 8 days after creation, not refreshed on hits.
haiku-low.q6: Consumption pauses rather than failing open, so lag grows and alerts fire. No duplicates get through. The brief does not say what clients see.
haiku-low.q7: Planned ledger rows are retried with their exact recorded offset range, and each load is one transaction that appends rows and marks them loaded. Loaded rows are skipped, and dedup returns the same winner for the same record.
haiku-low.q8: Replay reads only the raw archive in object storage, for days D-8 through D. Rebuilt events are written to a staging table or location named by run ID, which dashboards cannot see.
haiku-low.q9: It scans raw days D-8 through D, treats same partition and offset as one record, keeps the lowest (partition, offset) copy per event_id, and keeps it only if received_at is in day D.
haiku-low.q10: No swap happens, so the live partition stays untouched and the swap is atomic. The run is marked failed, the lock is released, and the operator fixes the cause and resubmits. A bad swap is rolled back from backup.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed days, those with a closed marker, no older than 82 days, and with no other replay holding the lock for that day.
haiku-low.q12: Undecided. Product must choose whether bot traffic is dropped or kept with an is_suspected_bot flag. The plan does not choose, and the raw archive keeps all events either way.

sonnet.q1: Valid events are accepted and malformed ones (missing event_id/device_id, or over 32 KB) are rejected individually, listed with reasons in the response body. It returns 202 only after every accepted event in the batch has been acknowledged by the log (all in-sync replicas).
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes. Mobile keeps unacknowledged events on the device up to 7 days, so retries can arrive up to 7 days later. Duplicates are removed by dedup.
sonnet.q3: The winner: the copy with the lowest offset in its partition, i.e. the first copy durably accepted. The later copy is dropped from events_clean (it stays in the raw archive). The event stays in its first day.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday. The day is the UTC day of received_at (00:10 Tuesday); the client timestamp is never used. It goes to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay.
sonnet.q5: In the key-value store, keyed by event_id, with the value being the record's partition:offset. Entries are removed by a per-key TTL of 8 days from creation, not refreshed on later hits.
sonnet.q6: The live processor pauses consumption and does not fail open. Clients' events still get appended to the log (collector is independent), but lag grows and alerts fire, breaching the 5-minute target visibly instead of letting duplicates through.
sonnet.q7: A load ledger records each batch's partition, offset range and day as planned before loading. The load is one warehouse transaction that appends rows and sets the status to loaded. On restart, planned rows are retried with exactly the recorded range, loaded rows are skipped, so no loss and no double insert. Dedup redelivery: if the key holds the record's own partition:offset it is treated as winner again, giving the same winners. Consumer offset is committed only after all ledger rows are loaded or dead-lettered.
sonnet.q8: Input is only the raw archive in object storage (days D-8 through D); no log, no key-value store. Rebuilt events are written to a staging table or location named by the run ID, which dashboards cannot see.
sonnet.q9: It builds its own dedup from the archive. It reads D-8 to D, treats records with the same (partition, offset) as one, and for each event_id picks the copy with the lowest (partition, offset). It keeps the event only if that winning copy's received_at is in day D, so an event first received on an earlier day and resent on D is dropped.
sonnet.q10: No swap happens when validation fails, so the live partition for D is untouched. The run is marked failed with the reason in the run ledger, the submitting operator is notified, an alert fires and the lock is released. The operator fixes the cause and resubmits; staging data stays for inspection until its retention ends. If a bad swap already happened, roll back by atomically replacing the partition from the backup.
sonnet.q11: Closed days only (those with the closed marker, closing after 02:00 UTC on D+1), no older than 82 days, and with no other replay holding the lock for that day.
sonnet.q12: Undecided (OPEN); product must decide before the bot stage is built. Either bots are dropped from events_clean (bot classifier version becomes part of the enrichment version, replay row counts account for it) or kept with an is_suspected_bot flag column. The raw archive keeps them either way, and replay applies the same policy as live.
